The two mandates
## Adopt AI at all costs. Trust nothing by default.
Defense and intelligence run under both orders at once — and so does every enterprise board. One demands speed, the other demands proof. They stay at odds only as long as your AI is a black box.
Mandate 01 · Velocity
### Field AI now.
Frontier models in production, agents in the workflow, capability compounding monthly. Falling behind is the unacceptable risk.
Mandate 02 · Verification
### Prove every action.
Every identity verified, every access scoped, every movement of data accounted for. An unexamined system is the unacceptable risk.
Sovereign AI is the bridge
### Bring your AI. Bring your data. Own everything in between.
Both run inside your boundary, on one governed plane — so the black box becomes an execution graph you can interrogate, and zero trust becomes something you enforce rather than assume.
Speed you can prove. Trust you can enforce.
[Mission intelligence Autonomous intelligence for classified networks and accredited environments. Defense, intelligence, and civilian agencies — missions where security and trust are non-negotiable. One platform — proven commercially, deployed in classified. No black box, no vendor lock-in.
Whatever the data, wherever it must remain — continuously AI-ready.
Why sovereign
## Built for data that can never leave.
### Deploy anywhere
Cloud, hybrid, on-prem, or fully air-gapped. Same codebase across the full spectrum — accreditation follows the deployment, not the other way around.
### Model custody
Your data, your models, your weights — trained and served inside your boundary. No callbacks, no external model APIs, no telemetry.
### Zero trust by design
Identity-bound access, least-privilege boundaries, auditable data movement. Every action attributable, every credential scoped.
### Open by design
Model-agnostic and composable. Run any model or agent — Syntasa's own or the customer's — and swap either without re-platforming.
[Visit the Trust Center →](https://syntasa.com/trust-center)
